slides.title: Agent, loop, hearing and memory
slides.source: Source: Chapter 14, “Ideas you need” and the guard hands-on; Game AI Made Easy (agents); glossary, Game AI.
slides.notes: Guard and player positions are computed tick by tick at 30 ticks a second. Distances, the 200 px rule and the 1.0 s search are inputs. The hearing radius (250 px) and sight (380 px) are illustrative inputs.
slides.picture: A patrolling guard, then the same guard running a sense-decide-act loop against a walking player, then a noise ring reaching two of three guards, then a guard walking to the last place it saw the player.

needs a clear line to the target
An agent is a character that decides for itself. This one patrols between two waypoints at 100 px/s.

slides.title: Steering: velocity, seek, flee and arrive
slides.source: Source: Chapter 1, “Velocity”; glossary, Game AI (Steering, Seek, Flee, Arrive); Game AI Uncovered Vol. 2.
slides.notes: Steering is desired velocity minus current velocity, limited to 320 px/s² per tick; speed is capped at 160 px/s. 60 ticks a second.
slides.picture: An agent turning toward a target with its velocity and steering arrows, then seek overshooting, then flee stopping at a safe distance, then arrive slowing to a stop.

new_texts: Behaviours that adjust movement toward a goal.
Speed with a direction; max speed caps its size.
aims at the target and never slows
same aim, but speed drops near the target
grey = desired · black = current velocity · red = steering
Steering = desired velocity minus current velocity, limited per tick. Velocity is speed with a direction; speed stays at or below 160 px/s.

slides.notes: Pursue uses the prediction distance / chaser speed. Wander is seeded (seed 33).
slides.picture: A chaser that seeks lags behind a moving target while a chaser that pursues cuts it off; then an agent wandering with a small circle ahead of it.

new_texts: Steer toward where a moving target will be.
aims at where the target is now
aims at where it will be
seek catches at 3.0 s · pursue catches at 2.6 s (both 110 px/s)
The target (black) runs at a steady 63 px/s. Pursue predicts its position after the travel time, so it catches it 0.4 s sooner than seek.

slides.title: Breadth-first search, Dijkstra and the open and closed set
slides.source: Source: glossary, Game AI (Dijkstra); Game AI Made Easy.
slides.notes: Mud costs 8. Breadth-first ignores cost; Dijkstra respects it.
slides.picture: The same room searched by breadth-first search, then by Dijkstra, with the cells they expand shaded, then a frozen mid-search view showing the open and closed sets.

new_texts: Expands outward one step at a time and ignores cost.
Breadth-first spreads one step at a time and stops at the goal. It takes the fewest steps (11) but the route crosses mud: cost 18.
all_texts: Expands outward one step at a time and ignores cost.
Breadth-first spreads one step at a time and stops at the goal. It takes the fewest steps (11) but the route crosses mud: cost 18.

new_texts: Pathfinding that expands by cost so far only, with no heuristic.
Dijkstra always expands the open cell with the lowest cost so far. It avoids the mud: cost 15, though 15 steps.
all_texts: Expands outward one step at a time and ignores cost.
Pathfinding that expands by cost so far only, with no heuristic.

Open = found but not yet expanded (red outline). Closed = expanded and done (pink). The search ends when the goal is taken from the open set.

slides.title: Manhattan, Euclidean and admissible heuristics
slides.source: Source: glossary, Game AI (Manhattan distance, Admissible heuristic).
slides.notes: Second room has a mud column of cost 8; the start and goal are on the same row.
slides.picture: A staircase of grid moves between two cells, then the straight line between them, then two A* runs on a room with mud: one with an honest estimate and one with the estimate multiplied by four.

new_texts: Distance counted along grid axes only.
Manhattan distance counts moves along grid axes: 5 across plus 3 up is 8. On a grid that moves in four directions it is the true cost when nothing is in the way.
all_texts: Distance counted along grid axes only.
Manhattan distance counts moves along grid axes: 5 across plus 3 up is 8. On a grid that moves in four directions it is the true cost when nothing is in the way.

new_texts: never above the true cost of 8 moves
Euclidean distance is the straight line, 5.83. It is never more than Manhattan, so it never overestimates, but on a four-direction grid it is the weaker guide.
all_texts: Distance counted along grid axes only.
never above the true cost of 8 moves
Euclidean distance is the straight line, 5.83. It is never more than Manhattan, so it never overestimates, but on a four-direction grid it is the weaker guide.

new_texts: An estimate that never overestimates the true cost.
h × 4 reaches the goal after 10 expansions instead of 21,
but pays 21 where the honest estimate pays 13.
An admissible heuristic never overestimates, and A* then returns the cheapest path. Inflate it and A* hurries into the mud: faster, but not cheapest.

slides.title: NavigationAgent2D, path smoothing and local avoidance
slides.source: Source: Chapter 14, “Navigation: a server, a region, an agent”; glossary, Game AI (NavigationAgent2D, Local avoidance).
slides.notes: Smoothing keeps only the corners where a straight line between cell centres would cross a wall.
slides.picture: An agent following a path of cells to the target with the next path position marked, then the raw cell path beside its smoothed version, then two agents on a head-on course, one pair without avoidance and one with.

new_texts: Godot node that follows a navmesh path.
reacts to what is close, each tick
THE AGENT ASKS FOR THE NEXT POINT EVERY FRAME
Set target_position; the server returns a path. Each physics frame the agent asks get_next_path_position() and moves toward it. The agent does not move the body itself.
all_texts: Godot node that follows a navmesh path.
reacts to what is close, each tick
THE AGENT ASKS FOR THE NEXT POINT EVERY FRAME
Set target_position; the server returns a path. Each physics frame the agent asks get_next_path_position() and moves toward it. The agent does not move the body itself.

new_texts: Cut corners from a path wherever the straight line is clear.
A cell path turns at every cell. Smoothing keeps a corner only where the straight line would hit a wall: 15.0 cells becomes 14.1.

slides.title: Before you trust a game AI behaviour
slides.picture: A checklist of six items drawn one at a time.

Is the steering right: seek, arrive, pursue or flee?
Does it slow down and stop where it should?
Is the map a grid, a mesh or waypoints, and why?
Is the search A* with a heuristic that never overestimates?
Is every random choice seeded, so a test can replay it?
Then say it exactly: not “make it smart”, but “within 340 px, 70° cone, seed 5”.
